The Discourse on Decline:
Loss through Argumentation.
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then in every case an Arahant falls away from Arahantship?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is it the case that in every instance an Arahant falls away from Arahantship?
Yes. Is there, then, a falling away from Arahantship in every instance for an Arahant?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
Is it the case that an Arahant always falls away from Arahantship?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is it the case that an Arahant always falls away from Arahantship?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is there, then, always a falling away from Arahatship?
“One should not say so” … [and so on] …
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
Do all Arahants fall away from Arahantship?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Do you maintain that all Arahants fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
Is it the case that all Arahants undergo falling away?
One should not say so … [as before] … Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Does an Arahant, falling away from Arahantship, fall away from the four fruits?
[The respondent replies: “One should not say so…” [and so on].
If a merchant, while exercising his status as a merchant with four hundred thousand [kahāpaṇas], were to lose one hundred thousand, would he thereby be deprived of his status as a merchant?
Yes, he would.
Would he then be deprived of his entire fortune?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it possible that a guild-leader,
while exercising his leadership over four hundred thousand [members], would be liable to fall away from all his property when one hundred thousand have been lost?
Yes, it is.
Is an Arahant, falling away from Arahantship, capable of falling away from the four fruits?
One should not say so… [as before]… The Falling Away of Noble Persons in Comparison.
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.

It should not be said so ... [as before] ...

One should not say so… [as before] … Does an arahant fall away from arahantship?
“Yes,” [you say].

You should not say so … [and so on] … No, indeed.
Does a non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning? Yes.
Does a stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does a non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning? Yes.
Does a once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
One should not say so… [as before] … Does a once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
“Yes,” you say.
“Does a stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
You must not say so… [and so on].
Does one who has entered the stream not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes. Does an Arhat not fall away from Arhatship? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does a once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-returning? Yes.
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Does a Non-returner fall away from the fruit of Non-returning? One should not say so.
“Yes,” [you say].

You should not say so … [and so on] … No, indeed.
Does one who has entered the stream not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes. Does one who is a non-returner not fall away from the fruit of non-returning? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does a once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-returning? Yes.
Does a non-returner not fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
One should not say so… [as before] … Does a stream-enterer not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry? One should not say so.
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Does a once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
“One should certainly not say so,” … [and so on].
Does an arahant fall away from arahantship? Yes.
When an arahant falling away from arahantship comes to rest where?
Regarding the fruit of non-returning:
if a non-returner, falling away from the fruit of non-returning, where does he stand?
He stands at the fruit of once-returning.
“Where does one who is a once-returner, falling away from the fruit of once-returning, come to rest?
“In the fruit of stream-entry.
“Does one who is a stream-enterer, falling away from the fruit of stream-entry, come to rest on the plane of an ordinary person?”
It should not be stated thus.
Understand the refutation:
If an Arahant, falling away from Arahantship, is established in the fruit of Non-returning, then a Non-returner, falling away from the fruit of Non-returning—
One stabilizes at the fruit of once-returning; a once-returner, falling away from the fruit of once-returning, stabilizes at the fruit of stream-entry.
Therefore, indeed, it should be said:
"A stream-enterer, falling away from the fruit of stream-entry, stabilizes on the level of an ordinary person."
Is it the case that an Arahant, falling away from Arahantship, is established in the fruit of stream-entry? Yes.
Does he, immediately after the fruit of stream-entry, realize Arahantship itself?
It should not be said thus ... [as before] ...
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
Does a stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Of whom are the defilements more abandoned: of the Arahant or of the stream-enterer?
Of the Arahant.
If more defilements have been abandoned by the Arahant, yet the Arahant falls away from arahantship, then indeed, sir, you must say this: [that there are still remaining defilements].
“One who has entered the stream falls away from the fruit of stream-entry.
Does one who is an Arhat fall away from Arhatship? Yes.
Does a once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Of whom are more defilements abandoned: of an arahant or of a once-returner?
Of the Arahant.
If more defilements have been abandoned by the Arahant, yet the Arahant falls away from Arahatship,
then indeed, sir, you must admit this.
“One who has attained the fruit of once-returning falls away from the fruit of once-returning.
Does one who has attained the state of an arahant fall away from arahantship? Yes.
Does a non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Of whom are more defilements abandoned: of an Arahant or of a non-returner?
Of the Arahant.
If more defilements have been abandoned by the Arahant, yet the Arahant falls away from Arahatship, then indeed, sir, you must say this: [that the Arahant can fall away].
“One who has attained the state of a non-returner falls away from the fruit of non-returning.
Does one who has attained the state of a non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning? Yes.
Does one who has entered the stream fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Of whom are more defilements abandoned: of the non-returner or of the stream-enterer?
Regarding the non-returner:

if more defilements have been abandoned by the non-returner, yet the non-returner falls away from the fruit of non-returning, then indeed, sir, it must be said: [that the non-returner has not abandoned all defilements].
“One who has entered the stream falls away from the fruit of stream-entry,” it is said.
Does one who has attained the state of non-return fall away from the fruit of non-return?
Yes, he does.
Does a once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...Of whom are more defilements abandoned: of a non-returner or of a once-returner?
Regarding the non-returner:

if more defilements have been abandoned by the non-returner, yet the non-returner falls away from the fruit of non-returning, then indeed, sir, it must be said: [that the non-returner has not abandoned all defilements].
“One who has attained the fruit of once-returning falls away from the fruit of once-returning.
Does one who has attained the fruit of once-returning fall away from the fruit of once-returning? Yes.
Does a stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Of which one are there more defilements abandoned: the once-returner or the stream-enterer?
For a once-returner.

If more defilements have been abandoned by a once-returner, yet the once-returner falls away from the fruit of once-returning, then indeed it must be said: [that the once-returner has not abandoned all defilements].
“One who has entered the stream falls away from the fruit of stream-entry.
Does one who is an Arhat fall away from Arhatship? Yes.
Does one who has entered the stream fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so …pe… For whom is the cultivation of the path most intense: for the Arahant or for the stream-enterer?
Of the Arahant.
If there is an excessive cultivation of the path for an Arahant, yet the Arahant falls away from Arahantship,
then indeed, sir, you must admit this.
“One who has entered the stream falls away from the fruit of stream-entry,” it is said.
Does one who is an arahant fall away from arahantship?
Yes, [he does].
Does one who has entered the stream fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so …pe… For whom is there an excessive cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness …pe…?
The development of the right efforts...
the development of the bases of psychic power...
the development of the faculties...
Is the development of the powers...
the development of the factors of enlightenment [the practice] of an arahant or of a stream-enterer?
Of an arahant.
If the Arahant possesses an excessive cultivation of the factors of enlightenment (bojjhaṅga) and yet the Arahant falls away from Arahantship,
then indeed, sir, you must say:
"The stream-enterer falls away from the fruit of stream-entry."
Does an arahant fall away from arahantship? Yes.
Does a once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?

It should not be stated thus … [as before] … To whom does the superior cultivation of the path … [and so on] … the cultivation of the factors of enlightenment belong: to an Arahant or to a Sakadāgāmī?
Of an Arahant.
If there is an excessive cultivation of the factors of enlightenment for an Arahant, and yet the Arahant falls away from Arahantship,
then indeed, sir, you must admit this.
“One who has attained the fruit of once-returning falls away from the fruit of once-returning.
Does one who has attained the state of an arahant fall away from arahantship? Yes.
Does a non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
One should not say so …pe… for whom is there an intense cultivation of the path …pe…?
Is the cultivation of the factors of enlightenment [the concern] of an arahant or of a non-returner?
Of an arahant.
If there is an excessive cultivation of the factors of enlightenment for an arahant, does the arahant fall away from arahantship?
Therefore, indeed, it must be said:
“A non-returner falls away from the fruit of non-returning.
Does a non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
“Yes.
“Does a stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.

the cultivation of the factors of enlightenment most intense? For the non-returner or the stream-enterer?

then indeed, sir,
it must be said that a stream-enterer falls away from the fruit of stream-entry.
Does one who is a non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning? Yes.
Does one who is a once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?

[as before] ...To whom does the superior cultivation of the path...

then indeed, sir, you must admit this.
“One who has attained the fruit of once-returning falls away from the fruit of once-returning.
Does one who has attained the fruit of once-returning fall away from the fruit of once-returning? Yes.
Does one who has entered the stream fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so … [as before] … For whom is there the supreme cultivation of the path? … [as before] …
Is the development of the factors of enlightenment [exclusive] to the once-returner or the stream-enterer?
It belongs to the once-returner.
If the development of the factors of enlightenment is predominant in the once-returner, does the once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
Therefore, indeed, it must be said:

“Yes,” [you say].

“But has the view of a personal body (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*) been abandoned by one who has entered the stream (*sotāpanna*), and does such a stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
You should not say so … [and so on].
Is lust abandoned by the Arahant? Yes. Does the Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
Yes. Is doubt abandoned by the Stream-enterer? ... [and so on] ... Yes. Does he fall away from Stream-entry? Yes.
Adherence to rules and observances has been abandoned …pe… lust leading to states of deprivation has been abandoned …pe… hatred leading to states of deprivation has been abandoned …pe…
Is the delusion leading to the states of misery abandoned, such that a stream-enterer falls away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...the hatred of an arahant is abandoned... [and so on].
Delusion has been abandoned...
conceit has been abandoned...
views have been abandoned...
Doubt has been abandoned...
sloth has been abandoned...
restlessness has been abandoned...
Shame has been abandoned … [and so on] … fearlessness of wrongdoing has been abandoned; does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
The view of a personal body (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*) is abandoned by one who has entered the stream; does it follow that the stream-enterer falls away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Is fearlessness of wrongdoing (*anottappa*) abandoned by an Arahant; does it follow that the Arahant falls away from Arahantship?
“Yes, [it is so].
“Doubt has been abandoned by the stream-enterer … pe … adherence to rules and observances has been abandoned … pe …”
"Is it the case that when lust leading to the states of deprivation has been abandoned,
and likewise hatred leading to the states of deprivation has been abandoned,
and delusion leading to the states of deprivation has been abandoned, a stream-enterer falls away from the fruit of stream-entry?"
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is passion abandoned by an Arahant, yet does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
The view of a personal body (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*) has been abandoned by a once-returner (*sakadāgāmī*); does the once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
One should not say so.
Has lust (*rāga*) been abandoned by an arahant; does the arahant fall away from arahantship (*arahatta*)? One should not say so.
“Yes,” he replied.
“In a once-returner, doubt has been abandoned … [and so on] … the adherence to rules and observances has been abandoned.”
“Gross sensual lust has been abandoned...
gross ill will has been abandoned; does the once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
One should not say so... [and so on].
The fault of an Arahant has been abandoned … [and so on] … moral shamelessness has been abandoned; does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
Is the view of a personal body abandoned by a once-returner …pe… is gross ill will abandoned [by him], yet does the once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
One should not say so.
Lust has been abandoned by the Arahant; does the Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
Yes. Has the view of a self-body been abandoned by the Non-returner; does the Non-returner fall away from the fruit of Non-returning? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is lust abandoned by an Arahant? Yes. Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
In the non-returner, doubt is abandoned …pe… adherence to rites and rituals is abandoned … subtle sensual lust is abandoned …
Is ill-will associated with the subtle (aṇusahagata) abandoned [by him], and does the non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
One should not say so. Has hatred been abandoned by the Arhat? ... [and so on] ... [One should not say so].
Is fearlessness of wrongdoing abandoned [by an Arahant], such that an Arahant falls away from Arahantship?
Yes. Is the view of a personal body abandoned by a Non-returner …pe…? Yes.
Is ill will that is subtle (anu-sahagata) abandoned [by the non-returner], yet does the non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
One should not say so.
Is the view of a self-existent body (sakkāya-diṭṭhi) abandoned by the non-returner, yet does the non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning? One should not say so.
“Yes,” you say.
“Is the identity view abandoned by a stream-enterer? Does a stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
You must not say so.
Is the view of a personal body abandoned by a non-returner? Yes. Does a non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
Yes. Is doubt abandoned by a stream-enterer? ... [and so on] ... Yes. Does a stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry? Yes.
Is it not the case that the delusion leading to the states of misery has been abandoned, yet the stream-enterer falls away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so.
Has doubt been abandoned by the non-returner? ... [and so on] ... one should not say so.
Is ill-will that is subtle concomitant abandoned, and does the non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
Yes. Is the view of a personal body abandoned for one who has entered the stream? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
Delusion leading to rebirth in the states of misery has been abandoned; does the stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so.
Is the view of a personal body abandoned by the non-returner; does the non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning? One should not say so.
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Has the view of a self-identity been abandoned by a once-returner? Does a once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
One should not say so.
Is the view of a personal body abandoned by a non-returner? Yes. Does the non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
Yes. Is doubt abandoned by a once-returner? ... [and so on] ... Yes. Does the once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning? Yes.
"Has the clinging to rules and observances been abandoned...
has gross sensual lust been abandoned...
has gross ill will been abandoned, such that a once-returner falls away from the fruit of once-returning?"
It should not be said so.
Has doubt been abandoned by the non-returner?
…pe… has even subtle ill-will been abandoned? Does the non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
“Yes. “Then,
is the identity view abandoned by the once-returner … and is gross ill will abandoned, yet does the once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?”
It should not be said so.
Is the view of a personal body abandoned by a once-returner, yet does the once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
Yes, it is so.
The view of a personal body (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*) has been abandoned by the stream-enterer; does the stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so.
The view of a personal body has been abandoned by the once-returner; does the once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning? One should not say so.
“Yes,” he said.
“Is doubt abandoned by the stream-enterer?
… Is delusion leading to states of deprivation abandoned? Does the stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?”
It should not be said so.
For the once-returner, doubt has been abandoned... [and so on] ...
gross sensual lust has been abandoned.
Is coarse ill-will abandoned, and does the once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
Yes. Is the view of a self-identity abandoned for the stream-enterer … [and so on] …? Yes.
Delusion leading to rebirth in the states of misery has been abandoned; does the stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
One should not say so.
Is the view of a personal body abandoned by the stream-enterer; does the stream-enterer not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry? One should say so.
“Yes,” you say.
“The lust of an Arahant has been abandoned; does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
You must not say so.
Is the view of a personal body abandoned by one who has entered the stream, and does that stream-enterer not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes. Is hatred abandoned by an Arhat … [and so on] …? Yes.
“Is fearlessness of wrongdoing abandoned, yet does the Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
One should not say so.
“Is doubt abandoned by the stream-enterer … [and so on] …” [One should not say so.]
Is the delusion leading to the states of misery abandoned, such that a stream-enterer does not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes. Is the lust of an arahant abandoned … [and so on] …? Yes.
“Is fearlessness of wrongdoing abandoned, yet does the Arahant not fall away from Arahantship?
One should not say so.
“Is the view of a self-identity abandoned by a once-returner, yet does the once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-returning? One should not say so.
“Yes,” he said.
“The lust of an Arahant has been abandoned … [and so on] … even fearlessness of wrongdoing has been abandoned; does an Arahant not fall away from Arahantship?”
It should not be said so.
Has doubt been abandoned by the once-returner?
…pe… has gross ill-will been abandoned? Does the once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
“Yes,” he said.
“The lust of an Arahant has been abandoned … [and so on] … even cowardice has been abandoned; does an Arahant not fall away from Arahantship?”
It should not be said so.
Is the view of a personal body abandoned by a non-returner, and does the non-returner not fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
Yes, it should be affirmed.
“Is lust abandoned by the Arahant … [and so on] … is moral shamelessness abandoned by the Arahant, such that the Arahant does not fall away from Arahantship?
One should not say so.
In the non-returner, doubt is abandoned …pe… even subtle ill-will is abandoned;
does the non-returner not fall away from the fruit of non-returning? Yes.
"Is lust abandoned by the Arahant...
[and so on] ...is lack of moral dread abandoned by the Arahant, such that the Arahant does not fall away from Arahatship?
One should not say this.
Is the view of a personal body abandoned by one who has entered the stream, and does that stream-enterer not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?

Yes. Is the view of a personal body abandoned by one who is a non-returner … and is even the residual tendency toward ill will abandoned, and does that non-returner not fall away from the fruit of non-returning? Yes.
It should not be said so.
Has doubt been abandoned by the stream-enterer? ...pe...
has the delusion leading to states of deprivation been abandoned? Does the stream-enterer not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
“Yes, [it is so].

“Is the view of a personal body (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*) abandoned by a non-returner (*anāgāmī*) …pe… is even subtle ill-will (*byāpāda*) abandoned, and does the non-returner not fall away from the fruit of non-returning?”
It should not be said so.
Is the view of a real body abandoned by a once-returner, and does the once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
Yes, it is so.

Is it not the case that for a non-returner, personality-belief has been abandoned …pe… and even subtle ill-will has been abandoned, and thus the non-returner does not fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
It should not be said so.
In one who has attained the fruit of once-returning, doubt has been abandoned …pe… gross ill will has been abandoned; does such a once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
Yes.

Is it not the case that for a non-returner, personality-belief has been abandoned …pe… and even subtle ill-will has been abandoned, and yet the non-returner does not fall away from the fruit of non-returning?
One should not say so.
Is the view of a personal body abandoned by a stream-enterer, and does the stream-enterer not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes. Is the view of a personal body abandoned by a once-returner … [and so on] …? Yes.
"Coarse ill will has been abandoned; does the once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
One should not say so.
"Doubt has been abandoned by the stream-enterer... [and so on].
Is the delusion leading to the states of misery abandoned, so that the stream-enterer does not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes. Is the view of a personal body abandoned by the once-returner … [and so on] …? Yes.
Gross ill-will has been abandoned; does the once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-returning?
One should not say so.
Does the arahant fall away from arahantship? One should not say so.
“Yes.
“Is it not the case that for an Arahant, lust has been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and is of a nature not to arise again in the future?
“Yes.”

If, for an Arahant, lust has been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and is of a nature not to arise again in the future, then surely it should not be said:
"An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
“Yes.
“But has not hatred been abandoned by the Arahant? … pe … has delusion been abandoned?”
Pride has been abandoned...
views have been abandoned...
doubt has been abandoned...
Sloth has been abandoned...
restlessness has been abandoned...
moral shamelessness has been abandoned...
“Is lack of moral dread abandoned by the Arahant, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and subject to non-arising in the future?
“Yes.

“If lack of moral dread is abandoned by the Arahant, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, rendered non-existent, and subject to non-arising in the future, then indeed, sir, you should not say:”
“It is said that an arahant falls away from arahantship.
Does an arahant fall away from arahantship? Yes.
Is it not the case that the path for the abandoning of lust has been cultivated by the Arahant?
Yes, it has.
If the path for the abandoning of lust has indeed been cultivated by the Arahant, then surely you should not say this: [that he still possesses lust].
“One who is an Arahant falls away from Arahantship.
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
Is it not the case that for an Arahant the foundations of mindfulness have been developed for the abandoning of lust...
the right efforts have been developed...
the bases of psychic power have been developed?
Have the faculties been cultivated?
Have the powers been cultivated?
Have the factors of awakening been cultivated?
“Yes.
“If the factors of enlightenment have been developed for the abandoning of lust in an Arahant, then indeed, it should not be said:
‘An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.’”
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
Yes. But is it not the case that for an Arahant there is the abandoning of hatred... [and so forth]?
Is the path developed for the abandoning of fearlessness of wrongdoing … [and] are the factors of enlightenment developed? Yes.
If the factors of enlightenment have been developed for the abandoning of non-fearlessness by an Arahant, then surely it should not be said:
"An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
“Yes, [he does].

“Is it not the case that an Arahant is one who is free from lust, free from hatred, and free from delusion; one who has done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, completely liberated through final knowledge, whose crossbar has been lifted, whose moat has been filled in, whose pillar has been uprooted, who is without bars, noble, and whose banner is lowered?”
Has he laid down the burden, is he detached, and has he won the victory of a well-conquered foe?
Has he fully understood suffering, abandoned its origin, realized its cessation, and cultivated the path?

Has he directly known what is to be directly known, fully understood what is to be fully understood, abandoned what is to be abandoned, cultivated what is to be cultivated, and realized what is to be realized?
“Yes.
“If it is true that an Arahant is free from lust, free from hatred,
and free from delusion … [and so on] … that what is to be realized has been realized, then indeed, sir, you should not say:”
“An arahant falls away from arahantship.
Does an arahant fall away from arahantship?
(…) An arahant who is liberated by occasion falls away from arahantship; an arahant who is not liberated by occasion does not fall away from arahantship.
Does an arahant who is liberated by occasion fall away from arahantship?
Yes. Does an arahant who is liberated non-occasionally fall away from arahantship? Yes.
It should not be said so.
Is it not the case that an arahant who is liberated at all times does not fall away from arahantship?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that an arahant who is liberated by occasion does not fall away from arahantship?
One should not say so.
Is passion abandoned by an arahant who is liberated by occasion? Does an arahant who is liberated by occasion fall away from arahantship?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Is lust abandoned by an arahant who is liberated at all times (asamayavimutta), and does an arahant liberated at all times fall away from arahantship?
“One should not say so.”

In the case of an arahant who is liberated by occasion, hatred is abandoned … [and so on] … lack of moral dread is abandoned. Does such an arahant, liberated by occasion, fall away from arahantship? Yes.
In the case of an arahant who is liberated at all times (asamayavimutta), shamelessness has been abandoned; does such an arahant, liberated at all times, fall away from arahantship?
One should not say so.

In the case of an arahant who is liberated occasionally (samayavimutta), the path has been cultivated for the abandoning of lust; does such an arahant, liberated occasionally, fall away from arahantship?
“Yes,” you say.
“Has the path been developed by an arahant liberated at all times for the abandoning of lust? Does an arahant liberated at all times fall away from arahantship?
You must not say so.
For an arahant liberated by occasion, the foundations of mindfulness have been developed for the abandoning of lust...
the right endeavors have been developed...
the bases of psychic power have been developed... [and so on].
If the faculties have been developed...
the powers have been developed...
the factors of enlightenment have been developed, can an arahant who is liberated by occasion fall away from arahantship?
“Yes.
“Then for an arahant liberated at any time, the foundations of mindfulness have been developed for the abandoning of lust … [and so on] … the factors of enlightenment have been developed;
yet does that arahant liberated at any time fall away from arahantship?”
It should not be stated thus.
For the arahant liberated by occasion, the path has been developed for the abandoning of hatred … [and so on] … for the abandoning of moral shamelessness … [and so on] … moral recklessness.
Is it the case that an arahant who is liberated by occasion (samaya-vimutta), having developed the factors of enlightenment, falls away from arahantship?
Yes. [If so,] has the path for abandoning lack of moral dread been developed by an arahant who is not liberated by occasion? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
If the factors of enlightenment have been developed, does an Arahant who is liberated at all times fall away from that Arahantship?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
An Arahant who is liberated by occasion is one who is free from lust, free from hatred, and free from delusion; one who has done what was to be done, laid down the burden, and attained his own goal.

With the fetters of existence utterly destroyed, liberated through right knowledge, with the crossbar lifted, the trench filled in, the pillar uprooted, free from the bolt, the noble one whose banner is lowered, whose burden is laid down, detached, a victor who has won a well-fought victory—for him suffering is fully understood, its origin abandoned, its cessation realized, and the path cultivated;
what was to be directly known has been directly known, and what was to be fully understood... [has been fully understood].
If the fully understood is fully understood, the abandonable is abandoned, the to-be-developed is developed, and the to-be-realized is realized,
does an Arahant liberated by occasion fall away from that Arahantship? Yes.
The Arahant who is liberated at all times is free from lust, free from hatred, and free from delusion...
[as before] ...he has realized what was to be realized. Does such an Arahant, liberated at all times, fall away from Arahantship?
One should not say so.
Is passion abandoned by an arahant who is liberated at all times, and does that arahant, liberated at all times, not fall away from arahantship? Yes.
Is passion abandoned by an arahant who is liberated occasionally, and does that arahant, liberated occasionally, not fall away from arahantship?
It should not be said so.
Has the hatred of an arahant liberated at any time been abandoned? ...
[and so on] ... has fearlessness of wrongdoing been abandoned? Does an arahant liberated at any time fall away from arahantship?
“Yes,” you say.
“Has fearlessness of wrongdoing been abandoned by an arahant who is liberated by occasion? Does an arahant liberated by occasion not fall away from arahantship?
You must not say so.
For an arahant who is liberated at all times, the path has been developed for the abandoning of lust … [and so on] … the factors of enlightenment have been developed;
does that arahant, liberated at all times, not fall away from arahantship? Yes.
If the path has been developed for the abandoning of lust by an Arahant who is occasionally liberated,
and the factors of enlightenment have been developed, does it follow that the Arahant who is occasionally liberated does not fall away from Arahantship?
One should not say so.

For an arahant liberated at all times, has the path been developed for the abandoning of hatred … pe … for the abandoning of lack of moral dread … pe … have the factors of enlightenment been developed,
such that the arahant liberated at all times does not fall away from arahantship?
“Yes.
“If the path has been developed for the abandoning of lack of moral dread in an arahant liberated by occasion,
and likewise the factors of enlightenment have been developed, does that arahant liberated by occasion not fall away from arahantship?”
It should not be said so.

Is an arahant liberated at all times, free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion … [as before] … who has realized what was to be realized, and does not fall away from the state of an arahant liberated at all times? Yes. (A III 352)
“Yes.

“An arahant liberated by occasion is free from lust, free from hatred, and free from delusion … [as before] … he has realized what was to be realized. Does an arahant liberated by occasion not fall away from arahantship?”
It should not be said so … [as before] … Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
Did the elder Sāriputta fall away from arahantship?
One should not say so.
[The same applies to] the elder Mahāmoggallāna...
The Elder Mahākassapa … the Elder Mahākaccāyana … the Elder Mahākoṭṭhika …
Did the elder Mahāpanthaka fall away from arahantship?
One should not say so.
Did the elder Sāriputta not fall away from arahantship? One should say so.
“Yes.
“If the Elder Sāriputta did not fall away from arahantship, then indeed it should not be said:
‘An Arahant falls away from arahantship.’”
The elder Mahāmoggallāna … the elder Mahākassapa … the elder Mahākaccāyana …
Did the elder Mahākoṭṭhika and the elder Mahāpanthaka not fall away from arahantship?
Yes, they did.
If the Elder Mahāpanthaka did not fall away from Arahatship, then indeed it should not be said:
"An Arahant falls away from Arahatship.
This concludes the Concordance of Noble Persons.
The Refutation of the Proof by Sutta:
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“For manifold indeed is the path proclaimed by the ascetic”?
"They do not go to the further shore with a double quality;
this is not understood as having a single quality.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes.
In that case, it should not be said:
“An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.”
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
Yes. Is there anything to be cut that has already been cut? No.
It should not be said so.
Is there cutting of what has already been cut?
Yes, it should be affirmed.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Free from craving, without grasping,
for whom there exists no duty;”
"For that which is cut off, there is no further cutting;
the flood and the snare have been uprooted.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes,” [he said].
“In that case, it should not be said:
‘There is cutting of what has already been cut.’”
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
Yes. Is there an accumulation of what has been done? Yes.
It should not be said so.
Is there an accumulation of what has been done? Yes.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
"Of that bhikkhu who is rightly liberated, whose mind is at peace..."
For him there is no accumulation,
nothing further to be done;
like a solid mass of rock, he stands firm.
It is not stirred by the wind;
even so are forms, tastes, sounds,
smells, and tangibles in their entirety.
Desirable things and undesirable things do not shake one who is such-like;
his mind is steady and utterly liberated.
"And we shall observe her.
Is this indeed a Sutta?
Yes, it is.
In that case, it should not be said:
"There is an accumulation of what has been done.
It should not be said.
“Does an arahant fall away from arahantship?”—
“Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Bhikkhus, these five things lead to the decline of a bhikkhu who is temporarily liberated.
What are the five?
Delight in work, delight in talk, delight in sleep, delight in company, and not reviewing one’s mind as it is liberated.”
“Monks, these five things lead to the decline of a monk who is liberated by occasion.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
"In that case, does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship?
"Is it to be said that an Arahant delights in action? "Certainly not."
Is it the case that an Arahant delights in action? Yes.
Is it the case that an Arahant has lust, sensual lust, obsession by sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, and the hindrance of sensual desire?
It should not be said so.
Is there in an arahant a delight in talk? Is there in an arahant a delight in sleep? Is there in an arahant a delight in company?
It should not be said so.
Is there in an Arahant a delight in society? Yes.
Is there in an Arahant lust, sensual lust, obsession by sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, and the hindrance of sensual desire?
It should not be said so.
Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes.
When an Arahant falls away from Arahantship, by what obsession does he fall away?
He falls away by being obsessed by lust.
Dependent upon what does that obsession arise?
"It arises dependent upon the underlying tendency.
Is it then to be said that an Arhat possesses underlying tendencies? Certainly not.
Is there a latent tendency in an Arahant? Yes.

Is there in an Arahant the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of views, the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of lust for existence, and the latent tendency of ignorance?
It should not be said thus.
"One who is obsessed by hatred declines" … [and so on] … "one who is obsessed by delusion declines" … [and so on].
"Dependent upon what does obsession arise?
"It arises dependent upon the underlying tendency.
"Does an arahant have an underlying tendency?"
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there a latent tendency (anusaya) in an Arahant? Yes.
Is there, for an Arahant, the underlying tendency to sensual lust …pe… the underlying tendency to ignorance?
One should not say so.
Does an arahant fall away from arahantship? Yes.
When an arahant is falling away from arahantship, what undergoes accumulation?
"Lust goes to accumulation.
[If this were so,] would it follow that "personality-belief goes to accumulation," "doubt goes to accumulation," and "adherence to rules and observances goes to accumulation"?
Certainly not; one should not say so.
“‘Hatred accumulates’ … ‘Delusion accumulates,’ ‘Personality-belief accumulates,’ ‘Doubt accumulates,’ or ‘Adherence to rules and observances accumulates’— should one not say this?
“One should not say so.”
Does an arahant fall away from arahantship?
Yes. Does an arahant accumulate [kamma]?
It should not be said so.
Should it be said that an arahant "destroys"?
It should not be said so.
Does an arahant abandon?
One should not say so. Does an arahant cling? One should not say so.
It should not be said so.
Should it be said that an arahant causes defilement?
It should not be said so.
"Does the Arahant cast out [the defilements]?
